description: 15 real production scenarios for pharma AI agents. Each maps to a Cedar policy in policies.yaml.

scenarios.name: Major protocol deviation — IRB must be notified first
scenarios.narrative: Clinical trial AI agent automatically records a major protocol deviation (patient received wrong dose). ICH E6 GCP requires IRB notification before closing this record.

context.deviation_description: Patient received 200mg instead of 100mg study drug

scenarios.leadership_talking_point: GCP violations in clinical trials can invalidate an entire trial dataset — years of work and hundreds of millions in investment. AGR enforces ICH E6 compliance at the agent layer.

scenarios.name: Protocol amendment blocked — sponsor approval required
scenarios.narrative: Site coordinator agent attempts to amend inclusion criteria for a Phase III trial. Any protocol amendment requires sponsor and IRB approval before it takes effect.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Unauthorized protocol amendments are a common FDA inspection finding. AGR routes every amendment through the sponsor approval workflow — with a timestamped audit trail.

scenarios.name: Patient enrolment blocked — trial at maximum capacity
scenarios.narrative: Recruitment agent attempts to enrol patient 501 into a trial capped at 500 participants. Over-enrolment invalidates statistical power calculations.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Over-enrolment in a clinical trial can require statistical reanalysis costing $2-5M. AGR enforces the enrolment cap as a hard policy — not a UI warning the agent ignores.

scenarios.name: Trial unblinding blocked — DSMB approval required
scenarios.narrative: Data analyst agent attempts to unblind treatment assignments for interim analysis. Only the Data Safety Monitoring Board is authorized to approve unblinding.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Unauthorized unblinding destroys trial integrity and constitutes scientific misconduct. AGR treats the DSMB flag as a hard gate — not a checkbox.

scenarios.name: Serious adverse event — cannot be closed without medical review
scenarios.narrative: Safety monitoring agent attempts to auto-close a serious adverse event case as 'not drug-related'. SAEs require physician review before closure.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Incorrectly closed SAEs are the #1 FDA 483 observation. AGR mandates physician sign-off on every serious event — the agent cannot auto-close regardless of its assessment.

scenarios.name: SUSAR submission blocked — outside 7-day reporting window
scenarios.narrative: Pharmacovigilance agent attempts to submit a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction report 9 days after awareness. EMA requires submission within 7 days — late submission carries regulatory penalty.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Late SUSAR submissions trigger automatic EMA review and can result in clinical hold. AGR blocks the late submission and flags it for expedited manual handling.

scenarios.name: Drug safety record deletion blocked within 15-year retention
scenarios.narrative: Data management agent attempts to archive old adverse event records from 2018 — only 6 years old. ICH E2F requires 15-year minimum retention for drug safety records.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Destroying drug safety records before 15 years is a GxP violation that can suspend a company's right to market the drug. AGR enforces retention as an immutable policy.

scenarios.name: NDA submission to FDA blocked — CMO sign-off missing
scenarios.narrative: Regulatory affairs agent prepares and attempts to auto-submit a New Drug Application to the FDA. CMO approval is mandatory before any regulatory submission.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Submitting an incomplete NDA to the FDA triggers a Refuse to File — setting drug approval back 12-18 months. AGR prevents the submission until the CMO has signed.

scenarios.name: eCTD modification blocked after regulatory freeze
scenarios.narrative: Document management agent attempts to update a module in the eCTD dossier after the submission date has been locked for FDA review.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Modifying a frozen regulatory submission corrupts the dossier and can invalidate the entire FDA review. AGR enforces the freeze as a hard block.

scenarios.name: Patient record access blocked — not part of treating team
scenarios.narrative: Research analytics agent attempts to access patient records for a patient not enrolled at its assigned site. HIPAA minimum necessary principle violated.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: HIPAA minimum necessary violations carry $1.9M maximum per violation category per year. AGR enforces treating-team membership checks — the agent cannot see what it should not see.

scenarios.name: Patient data sharing blocked — no consent on file
scenarios.narrative: Partner integration agent attempts to share patient biomarker data with a CRO partner. Patient has not provided data sharing consent.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Sharing genetic data without consent violates GDPR Article 9 and HIPAA simultaneously. AGR checks consent status before any data leaves your system.

scenarios.name: Bulk de-identification requires privacy officer approval
scenarios.narrative: ML agent attempts to de-identify 2,000 patient records for model training. Bulk de-identification processes require privacy officer oversight.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Flawed de-identification can still expose patient identity. AGR gates bulk de-identification behind privacy officer review — regardless of which agent requests it.

scenarios.name: Drug batch release blocked — QC not approved
scenarios.narrative: Manufacturing execution agent attempts to release a drug batch for distribution. QC analytical testing is still in progress.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Releasing an untested batch triggers FDA recall and criminal liability. AGR makes QC approval a mandatory gate — not a reminder the release agent can skip.

scenarios.name: Controlled substance dispensing requires dual approval
scenarios.narrative: Inventory management agent attempts to dispense Schedule II controlled substances from the lab. DEA regulations require dual-person integrity.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: DEA dual-person integrity for Schedule II substances is federal law. AGR enforces this in the AI agent layer — no single agent can dispense controlled substances alone.

scenarios.name: GxP audit trail modification blocked unconditionally (21 CFR Part 11)
scenarios.narrative: Maintenance agent attempts to correct timestamps in an electronic system audit trail. 21 CFR Part 11 mandates audit trails are never modified — only appended.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail integrity is the cornerstone of GxP computer system validation. AGR blocks this unconditionally — no context, no approval path, hard deny.
